item.title: Spotify hits 290m subscribers, posts second year of profit
item.description: Spotify has reported a global Premium subscriber base of 290 million paying users in the fourth quarter of 2025, alongside its second consecutive full year of operating profit, according to the company’s investor filing published on 10 February. The streaming platform added nine million net Premium subscribers in Q4, exceeding guidance by one million, bringing total net additions for the year to 27 million. item.title: Namibian singer Ms. Gideon joins Sony Music Africa
item.description: Sony Music Africa has signed Namibian singer‑songwriter Ms. Gideon (born Panduleni Gideon) through a partnership with ERA Music Group, marking the first time a recording artist from Namibia has joined the Sony Global Music Company roster. At 20 years old, the Windhoek‑born musician is recognised for her soulful voice, emotive songwriting, and a sound that blends soul, Afrobeats, and African musical influences. item.title: Nigeria: Wealth Official drops new single Time I’m On
item.description: Nigerian hip hop artist Wealth Official has released a new single titled ‘Time I’m On’, accompanied by visuals, which dropped last Friday. The track marks a new chapter in the artist’s career, emphasising focus, discipline, and a determined approach to his craft. Produced by Reid Put Me On, ‘Time I’m On’ is a hard-hitting hip-hop record characterised by sharp lyrics and a confident delivery. item.title: Graphic design internship opportunity at Music In Africa
item.description: The Music In Africa Foundation (MIAF) is seeking a talented Graphic Design Intern to join its team at the Rosebank office. One of the largest arts institutions on the continent, MIAF delivers a wide range of cultural and creative-sector development programmes across Africa. item.title: Zomba Arts Platform selected for regional digital heritage programme
item.description: Zomba Arts Platform (ZAP) has been chosen as Malawi’s implementing partner for Futures_Past: Amplifying Memory with Immersive Technologies, a regional initiative exploring new approaches to engaging with heritage through digital tools. The programme brings together cultural and archival institutions across Southern Africa to rethink how archival materials can be accessed, interpreted, and experienced. item.title: Wav Gardn’s Umdeni blends Afrocentric neo-soul with spiritual depth
item.description: Afrocentric neo-soul continues to gain momentum within Johannesburg’s alternative music scene, and Wav Gardn are among the emerging acts contributing to this shift. Their four-track EP, Umdeni, presents a concise body of work rooted in themes of African spirituality, resilience and renewal. The project opens with ‘Ithuba’, structured as a reflective appeal for guidance and opportunity. item.title: Open call: 2026 ACT Nyoloha Scholarship Programme
item.description: The Arts & Culture Trust (ACT) has opened applications for the 2026 Nyoloha Scholarship Programme, marking the fifth edition of the national initiative aimed at supporting emerging artists through funded tertiary study and professional development. The scholarship covers tuition and prescribed study materials only and supports studies in performing, visual and digital arts. item.title: Tyla to release second studio album A-Pop in March
item.description: South African singer Tyla will release her second studio album, A-Pop, on 15 March 2026, marking her first full-length project since winning the Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance. The forthcoming album arrives at a time of heightened international attention for the artist, who has become one of the most prominent African pop figures on the global stage. item.title: Behind the mic: Why radio producers are the quiet architects of connection
item.description: By Mzi Kaka Most listeners only hear the final product: the music, the banter, the seamless flow of conversation. What they do not hear is the architecture behind it. The radio producer is the invisible hand shaping the show long before the “On Air” light flickers to life. item.title: TikTok reportedly revising music royalty model to include per-play payments
item.description: TikTok is preparing to revise the way it pays music rights holders, according to information shared with Digital Music News (DMN), in a move that could significantly alter how royalties are calculated on the platform. Under TikTok’s existing system, rights holders are typically paid only for the initial use of a track in a video, regardless of how many times that video is viewed.
